Theme

Money, work & business · Household, washing & chores

rent noun

money paid for a house or flat

also rents, the rent, pay the rent, house rent

classical

Caes. BC 3.21.1: mercēdēs habitātiōnum annuās conductōribus dōnāvit
Cic. Att. 12.32.2: mercēdēs Argīlētī et Aventīnī, the rents from (his houses in) the Argiletum and on the Aventine
Traupman 370: mercēdem huic cellae dare, to pay the rent for this room

mercēs, mercēdis f.

noun, third declension

A house’s pay, as wages are a worker’s: mercēdēs habitātiōnum, the rents of dwellings. Cicero meant his son’s allowance at Athens to come out of the rents of two houses (Att. 12.32.2).

Other words

  • pēnsiō, pēnsiōnis f. — rent; a payment, an instalment

    noun, third declension · also used · classical · Suet. Ner. 44.2: pēnsiōnem annuam, a year’s rent; Juv. 9.63: pēnsiō clāmat, the rent cries out

    In Cicero a payment or instalment (see pay in instalments); rent in Suetonius and Juvenal (Lewis & Short). Not a pension (see pension).

  • habitātiō, habitātiōnis f. — house rent; properly a dwelling

    noun, third declension · also used · classical · Cic. Cael. 17: sūmptus ūnīus generis objectus est, habitātiōnis; Suet. Jul. 38.2: annuam etiam habitātiōnem … remīsit, he let them off a year’s rent

    What one pays for a dwelling: Caelius, said his accusers, lived at thirty thousand, trīgintā mīlibus habitāre (Cic. Cael. 17).

Examples

  • Sūmptus ūnīus generis objectus est, habitātiōnis; trīgintā mīlibus dīxistis eum habitāre. Nunc dēmum intellegō P. Clōdī īnsulam esse vēnālem, cujus hic in aediculīs habitat decem, ut opīnor, mīlibus.

    Only one kind of spending has been laid against him, his rent: you said he paid thirty thousand. Now at last I understand that Publius Clodius’s block of flats is up for sale: he lives in a little flat in it for ten thousand, I believe.Cic. Cael. 17

  • ūnam, quā mercēdēs habitātiōnum annuās conductōribus dōnāvit

    one (law), by which he let tenants off a year’s rentCaes. BC 3.21.1

  • mercēdem huic cellae dare

    to pay the rent for this roomTraupman 370

See also rent, landlord, tenant, house, pay, pay in instalments.
